p: brethren: The sixth part of this epistle containing different exhortations to stir up the Corinthians to liberality, with which the poverty of the church of Jerusalem might be helped at an appropriate time. And first of all he sets before them the example of the churches of Macedonia, which otherwise were brought by great misery to extreme poverty, so that the Corinthians should follow them.
grace of God bestowed on the: The benefit that God bestowed upon the Corinthians.
great trial of affliction the abundance: For those manifold afflictions with which the Lord tried them did not stop their joyful readiness, but also made it much more excellent and well-known.
willing of themselves: Of their own accord they were generous.
gift: He calls that "gift" which other men would have called a burden. And this verse is to be explained by 2Co 8:6.
And this they did: He amplifies the eagerness of the Macedonians in this, that they also desired Paul to stir up the Corinthians to accomplish the giving of alms by sending Titus to them again.
I speak not by commandment: Thirdly, he warns them to live up to the expectation which Paul and his companions have conceived of them.
forwardness of others: At the request of the Macedonians.
sincerity of your love: The naturalness of our love appears when we truly, and that frankly and freely, help our brethren even for Christ's sake.
For ye know the grace of: The fourth argument taken from the example of Christ.
And herein I give my advice: He takes good heed that he seem not to wrest it out of them by force, for unless it is voluntary, God does not accept it.

be forward a year ago: Not only to do, but also to do willingly: for he notes out of a ready willingness, without any enforcement by any other men. And much less did it come out of ambition and vain glory.
For if there be first a: Against those who excused themselves because they are not rich, as though it were only the duty of rich men to help the poor.
For I mean not that other: Christian liberality is mutual, so that one does not have too much, and the other to little.
equality: That as now in your abundance you help others with a share of your goods, so should others in the same way bestow some of their goods upon you.

But thanks be to God: He commends Titus and his two companions for many reasons, both that their credit might not be suspected, as though he had sent them slyly to rob the churches, and also so that they might be all the more ready to contribute.
in the gospel throughout all the: In the preaching of the Gospel.
grace: These alms which are bestowed for the relief of the church of Jerusalem.
abundance which is administered by us: In this plentiful liberality of the churches, which is committed to our trust.
brethren be enquired of: The two companions of Titus.
glory of Christ: By whom the glory of Christ is set forth.
churches: All the churches in whose presence you are in will be witnesses of this your godly behaviour, for these men are the messengers whom they have chosen by common consent, and sent to you.
